_claimLint: 2026-09-02: claim-lint in WARN mode for Butlery. It reports newly written prose that asserts something nothing measured — a universal quantifier, a number bound to a countable noun, an N-of-M, a file:line — when the same hunk carries no command deriving it. It runs at git commit and at Write/Edit, and blocks neither: it writes a systemMessage and appends a row to .claude/state/claim-lint-warnings.jsonl. Warn rather than block because this repo's measured rate is well above the repo the rules were calibrated against, and a gate that stops that share of commits gets switched off; the log is how a later decision to block gets evidence from THIS repo rather than from a replay. exemptPaths REPLACES the script's defaults rather than merging, so the inherited entries are restated here. The entries beyond them were each measured for their own effect before being added: two are dated decision records of the same class as an ADR, and adoption-status.md carries a generator banner in its own first lines saying to re-run the tool rather than hand-edit — a warning there would be unactionable by construction. Two files that LOOK exemptable are deliberately gated, on the advice of the session working here: ACCEPTED_LARGE_FILES.md and the Art. 30 retention registers record a MEASUREMENT of the code rather than a decision, and a measurement can rot — that session found stale numbers in both the day this was written. Nothing else suggested was added, because each removed no findings, and an exemption that removes nothing today is a blind spot tomorrow. tasks/todo.md is deliberately NOT exempt although it carries the largest share of findings: measured against each commit's parent, the great majority of those lines are newly written rather than old text moving down the file, and they are the kind this exists for — one names a source line number inside a plan document. Re-measure by driving hookMain with this config the way the hook does.

_reviewProof: 2026-08-01: proof of review moved from hand-written marker files to the RECORDED ledger. A marker was a separate act of writing performed by the party being audited — twelve were flagged as forged in one morning, and five of the six agents below never had a marker instruction at all, so the gate's own block message ('the agent writes it itself') taught blocked sessions to hand-write one. In ledger mode a PostToolUse hook records which reviewer read which bytes and a SubagentStop hook records the verdict it ended on; nothing is hand-writable and a later fix silently un-proves the file it touched. Reviewer agents MUST open files with Read and end on `REVIEW-VERDICT: pass|fail (N blocking)` — both are in each agent below. Do not set this in binge/webbkollen until their agents carry the same two rules; flipping first blocks every commit there.

reviewGates.//exact-agents: 2026-08-23, Malin's decision, mirroring the fix made in Synat the same day (c5ab880). The six `.claude/agents/<gate>.md` files are the INSTRUCTIONS each gate agent runs on, and they reached no gate at all. So a change that narrowed a reviewer's checklist — or emptied it — could be committed with no review, and the next review would run on the weakened instruction. Proven against the real hook in both directions: with the previous config the gate exits 0 and names nothing, with this one it exits 2 and names the file. COUPLED HALF, in this same commit: `.claude/agents/code-reviewer.md`'s `description:` line — what the dispatcher reads to decide whether to invoke the agent — now names the class, and the file gains a lens for it. Deliberately NOT the `*.knowledge*.md` files beside them: commit-gate reviewers run CONCURRENTLY and each records lessons into its own file, so gating them would ask one agent to read the post-edit bytes of files a sibling is still writing, and every review that records a lesson would cost a second round forever. ⚠ The residual is real: a knowledge file is read IN FULL before every review and carries do-not-re-file suppressors, so an edit there silences a finding class as effectively as deleting a checklist item, and only convention protects it. Deliberately code-reviewer only, so the push gate (`pushGate.agent`, which carries no `exact`) still never sees these files. ⚠ The gap that leaves is the SPLIT-ACROSS-BATCHES case: one batch widens the config, another edits the `description:` line, each commit gate sees half and no gate sees the pair. That matters more here than in Synat, because this repo's sprint engine commits batch by batch as its normal mode and the push gate is the only whole-range pass. Raised, not taken — Malin's decision. ⚠ STILL OPEN and not fixed here: `.claude/shared-plugin.json` itself reaches no gate in this repo. It is the file that decides which reviews apply at all, and Synat put it on this same list for that reason (BIN-696). Raised rather than widened, because it is a separate decision.

reviewGates._note: The whole-diff, cross-file pass. Was `codeReviewGate` until 2026-07-31, i.e. gated on the /code-review BUILTIN — a command only a human can start, so every unattended run (sprint-parallel, /commit, any resume) dead-ended asking Malin to type it. Same filePattern and same marker as before; the only change is that a spawnable agent now owns it. /code-review stays available and is still the deeper pass — it is simply no longer the ONLY way to earn this marker. NOTE the pattern is bare `\.dart$` on purpose: unlike the code-reviewer gate it does NOT exclude *.g.dart/*.freezed.dart, so a generated-only diff still meets a gate. Do not 'tidy' that exclusion in.

router._panelPolicy: Malin, 2026-08-13. Under the default 'block' the 2026-08-13 sprint selected six tickets, routed all six to a panel it cannot convene unattended, and shipped nothing — Butlery's remaining backlog is almost entirely Firestore rules and GDPR, so the tier gate now matches everything. 'park' builds those tickets and sends them to In Review for her instead of Done. The specialist reviewers (code-reviewer, firebase-backend-security, firestore-rules-tester, cloud-functions-specialist, integration-reviewer) still run on every commit and still hold a batch on failure; the panel is a second, slower layer, not the only one. Do NOT set this in binge/webbkollen without re-reading the dispatch-gate comment in sprint-execute-parallel.js — the earlier attempt at 'park' lost four of seven finished tickets because the commit-time backstop still held them.

delivery._cleanTreeIgnore: The agent .knowledge/.knowledge.archive files are written BY THE SPRINT'S OWN REVIEWER AGENTS mid-run (CLAUDE.md → Agents), so they are the run's noise, not a human's in-flight work. Left out until 2026-08-16, when two of them made the close-out read the tree as lost work and suppressed every Linear transition. Scoped to .claude/agents/ deliberately — a knowledge file is prose about principles and can never carry product code.
